Why money and inner peace can go together.

Kevin Trudeau explains the law of detachment: you can enjoy a beautiful house and fine cars and still feel free, as long as you are not attached to them.

He says materialism and spirituality are not opposites. The difference is attachment.

His axiom: love people and use things, instead of loving things and using people.

Which one do you catch yourself doing more often?

#ad #money #mindset #success #kevintrudeau

Why rich families hold on to old heirlooms.

Kevin Trudeau shares his belief that wealthy people keep special items at home, such as old artwork or a family heirloom, because they feel the energy of lucky, successful owners stays in the item.

It is his personal view, not a promise of any result.

Still, it raises a good question about the things we choose to surround ourselves with.

What object in your home carries a story that matters to you?

#ad #wealth #success #mindset #kevintrudeau

If someone can push your buttons, they steer your day.

Kevin Trudeau says that when you have a button to be pushed, everybody can affect you, like a puppet on a string.

He describes being an observer of your own life instead: you stop being at effect and start being at cause over your environment, which he links to a sense of control.

It is an idea about perspective, so notice how much of your day gets steered by other people's words.

Who pushes your buttons most often?
